problem_type: creation editor selection feedback disappearing on assistant focus
symptom: Selecting script text and focusing the creation assistant cleared the browser selection highlight even though the assistant still read and replaced the selected text correctly.
direct_cause: WorkbenchEditor published only selected text and a version counter; it did not retain the ProseMirror from/to range or render a focus-independent decoration after the browser moved focus to the assistant input.
class_root: The shared rich-text kernel had no explicit contract for selection ownership across a focus hand-off, so the browser's transient native selection was treated as the only visual representation while tool execution relied on an implicit editor selection.
affected_population: Creation users selecting script text before asking the assistant to revise it
Users who click, type, or attach context in the creation assistant before approving replace_selection
Any future creation editor action that hands focus to a sibling surface while retaining a document range
entry_points: Creation assistant read_selection and replace_selection tool execution
TextDocumentNode shared rich-text hook, explicitly not affected because it does not opt into the creation-only extension
internal_only_reason: The behavior is owned by Nomi's Tiptap/ProseMirror selection lifecycle and its creation-to-assistant focus hand-off. External editor documentation cannot decide which Nomi surface should retain a visual range.
invariants: A non-empty creation-editor selection remains visibly decorated after editor focus moves to the assistant.
Document transactions map the saved range so edits before it do not move the highlight to the wrong text.
A collapsed selection, replacement transaction, or document switch clears the stale decoration.
Canvas text nodes do not receive the creation-only persistent-selection extension.
The assistant read_selection and replace_selection tools continue to use the same editor selection and replacement path.

external_sources.purpose: Confirmed that Tiptap exposes the underlying ProseMirror state and transaction model used by the shared editor kernel.
Confirmed that inline decorations are focus-independent document-view annotations suitable for rendering a retained range.

recurrence.reason: Every sibling-surface focus hand-off can make a transient native selection disappear, and any future rich-text caller without a shared range contract could recreate the same visual failure.
same_class_scan: Scanned every useNomiRichTextEditor caller: WorkbenchEditor is the only feature-rich creation surface; TextDocumentNode is the separate canvas entry point and remains explicitly not affected.
Scanned all creation assistant read_selection and replace_selection paths and confirmed they consume the shared creation document tools rather than a second selection store.
Reproduced the real packaged workflow: native selection becomes empty after assistant focus, while replacement still lands at the original range.

generality_proof: The persistent-selection extension is installed at the shared rich-text hook boundary and is opt-in for the creation editor. The plugin maps every document transaction and clears every explicit collapsed or replacement selection, so all current and future creation focus hand-offs share the same behavior without changing the canvas text-node entry point.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the opt-in extension boundary so the creation editor receives persistent selection behavior while other rich-text callers do not.
Own range capture, transaction mapping, clearing, and focus-independent inline decorations for every creation selection hand-off.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The creation editor opts into PersistentSelectionExtension and its real Electron walkthrough verifies the decoration survives assistant focus.
The canvas caller passes no featureExtensions or persistent-selection option, preserving its existing selection and edit behavior.

prevention.invariant: A creation selection is represented by a mapped ProseMirror range and inline decoration until an explicit collapsed or replacement transaction clears it.
prevention.failure_mode: The plugin state becomes null and renders no decoration; focused unit tests and the creation Electron walkthrough fail before a stale or invisible selection can ship.
prevention.strategy: Move focus-independent selection ownership into one ProseMirror plugin and require the creation editor to opt into that shared boundary instead of relying on browser-native selection painting.

legacy_paths.rationale: There was no parallel selection store or legacy decoration path; the repair adds the missing shared representation and keeps the existing editor/tool protocol.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The defect is caused by Nomi's selection lifecycle contract, not by a Tiptap or ProseMirror dependency version.

migration: No stored document or tool protocol migration is required. The selection range and decoration are transient editor state and disappear when the editor unmounts or the selection is explicitly replaced.
residual_risks: A browser-native selection can still be empty by design; the decoration is the authoritative visual cue while the assistant owns focus.

If a future creation command intentionally keeps a non-empty selection after applying content, it must dispatch a collapsed selection or explicit clear transaction so stale decoration is not retained.
